text: {"features":[{"evidence":"multiple typos and misspellings","name":"Writing polish","description":"Captures how carefully edited and professionally presented the letter is at the sentence level.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Frequent spelling or typing errors distract from the content and suggest weak attention to detail."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains understandable and basically professional."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Only minor occasional slips appear; the letter reads as generally polished."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter is clean and well edited, with virtually no distracting copy errors."}]},{"evidence":"why this Core security role specifically","name":"Role-specific motivation","description":"Measures how clearly the letter explains attraction to this particular Google Information Security Engineering role rather than to software or security work in general.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives generic interest in a job, company, or field with little indication of why this role fits."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows broad interest in security, backend engineering, or Google, but with limited connection to this team's actual work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clearly connects the applicant's interests to this team's charter, such as security automation, vulnerability response, or AI agents."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Offers a sharp, distinctive rationale for this exact role, tied to Google's scale, Core context, and specific responsibilities."}]},{"evidence":"foundational infrastructure inherited by every team downstream","name":"Platform leverage orientation","description":"Captures whether the applicant is motivated by central infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains."}]},{"evidence":"make the secure path the easy path","name":"Developer enablement mindset","description":"Measures whether the applicant frames security engineering as helping developers succeed through good defaults and low-friction tooling.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not address how security work should interact with developer workflows."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Expresses a general desire to help teams, but without a clear enablement philosophy."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explicitly emphasizes secure defaults, reduced friction, or assisting engineers rather than adding process."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows a strong developer-enablement philosophy and backs it with language or examples of tooling that removed burden from engineers."}]},{"evidence":"Bachelor's or Master's or Doctoral degree","name":"Academic preparation","description":"Captures the formal depth of the applicant's stated academic background relevant to the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is stated."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"States a Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical preparation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States a Master's degree in a relevant field."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"States a doctoral degree or similarly advanced research training in a relevant field."}]},{"evidence":"3 years or 5 years or 7 years","name":"Professional tenure","description":"Measures the amount of hands-on software engineering experience the letter claims.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Shows less than the minimum experience or leaves tenure unclear."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows roughly entry-to-early-mid experience, around 2 to 3 years."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows established mid-level experience, around 4 to 6 years."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows 7 or more years of professional engineering experience."}]},{"evidence":"launched 2 or 4 or 6 production services","name":"Production delivery scope","description":"Captures how much repeated responsibility the letter shows for shipping and maintaining production systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides little or no evidence of shipping or maintaining production systems."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows limited but real delivery history, such as one or two production services."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows repeated production ownership, such as several services or launches."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows broad, repeated production delivery responsibility across many services."}]},{"evidence":"reworked a matching algorithm","name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"Measures whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering improvements.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no real evidence of data-structure or algorithm skill."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claims comfort with algorithms or data structures, but without a concrete example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives one specific example of using a better structure or algorithm to improve a system."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows especially strong algorithmic fluency through multiple examples or a clearly high-impact optimization on a critical problem."}]},{"evidence":"Python is production-grade","name":"Python depth","description":"Captures how central and mature the applicant's Python experience appears in services, tooling, or automation.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention Python, or only name-checks it without substance."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Uses Python mainly for light scripting or simple tooling."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows substantial Python use across services, automation, or internal systems."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents Python as a mature production language, with responsibility for important services or clearly engineered tooling."}]},{"evidence":"LLM-backed features with evaluation or hardening","name":"Applied AI maturity","description":"Measures the depth of real-world AI experience, especially whether it extends beyond experimentation into reliable production use.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No AI experience is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions AI or language models, but without clear production responsibility."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows direct experience shipping AI or LLM-backed features or workflows."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows production AI experience plus evidence of evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or other reliability controls."}]},{"evidence":"Python agents with Go guardrails","name":"Agentic architecture ownership","description":"Captures whether the applicant has designed agent-based systems and how thoughtfully they describe control boundaries around them.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention agentic systems or multi-step autonomous tooling."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions agents only vaguely or as a buzzword."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes building agentic systems that pair Python agents with Go back-end services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows clear ownership of agent design, emphasizing bounded actions, permissions, auditing, contracts, or guardrails."}]},{"evidence":"automated vulnerability triage queue","name":"Vulnerability workflow automation","description":"Measures direct experience building software that automates intake, classification, routing, or handling of vulnerability reports.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no evidence of automating vulnerability-handling workflows."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows interest in security automation, but no direct example involving vulnerability intake or triage."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Provides a direct example of building tooling for vulnerability intake, triage, routing, or deduplication."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes a substantial vulnerability pipeline that clearly reduced manual work through classification, prioritization, routing, or self-service."}]},{"evidence":"performed security assessments or led security reviews","name":"Security assessment ownership","description":"Captures the depth of hands-on security review work the applicant claims, from basic threat modeling to leading attacker-minded assessments.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of doing security assessments or reviews."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions security reviews or threat models lightly, with limited ownership."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows real hands-on assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, or structured security validation."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows strong ownership, such as leading reviews, assessing systems beyond their own code, or explaining a clear attacker-minded method."}]},{"evidence":"OSCP or Security+","name":"Security credential strength","description":"Measures whether the letter provides external security validation and how hands-on or demanding that credential appears to be.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No security certification is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a baseline certification that signals general security knowledge, such as Security+."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Mentions a hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP or an equivalent practical certification."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Pairs a strong hands-on credential with context about what was demonstrated, making the signal more credible and specific."}]},{"evidence":"capture-the-flag competitions","name":"Offensive practice","description":"Captures ongoing engagement with adversarial security practice outside ordinary software development work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No offensive-security practice is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions occasional CTF participation or similar practice."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular or serious participation in CTFs or comparable adversarial exercises."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows standout offensive practice, such as near-top or top placements in substantial competitions."}]},{"evidence":"maintainer of an open-source project","name":"Open-source stewardship","description":"Measures whether the applicant shows responsibility for public code, contributors, releases, or upstream fixes.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No open-source activity is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions occasional upstream patches or small contributions."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows responsibility for maintaining a project, library, or recurring release process."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows full stewardship of an externally used project, including reviews, releases, roadmap, or community interaction."}]},{"evidence":"distributed task queue or replicated cache side project","name":"Personal project ambition","description":"Captures the technical ambition of self-directed projects described outside the applicant's day job.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No personal project is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems."}]},{"evidence":"specific recent examples and outcomes","name":"Evidence specificity","description":"Measures how often the letter backs claims with concrete recent examples rather than generic assertions.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Relies mostly on abstract claims, adjectives, or requirement-matching language with little proof."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Includes some specifics, but much of the letter remains generic or unsupported."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Uses several concrete examples to anchor the main claims."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Consistently substantiates claims with recent, relevant examples and at least some indication of what changed or improved."}]},{"evidence":"someone always inherits what we build","name":"Maintainability orientation","description":"Captures whether the applicant explicitly thinks in terms of long-term operability, inheritance, and maintainable system design.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Shows no explicit concern for maintainability or long-term ownership."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions maintenance only as background experience, not as a design value."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explicitly values maintainability, operational ownership, or the fact that systems outlive their creators."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows a strong maintainer philosophy that clearly shapes how the applicant designs systems and why the role fits."}]},{"evidence":"quiet resilience rather than visible spectacle","name":"Security rigor philosophy","description":"Captures whether the letter articulates a principled view of security engineering as unusually high-standard, dependable work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Offers no distinct philosophy about the quality bar required for security engineering."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Makes only generic statements about reliability or security importance."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Expresses a clear philosophy of quiet resilience, dependable systems, or a higher standard for security tooling."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Builds a memorable, well-integrated case that security tooling demands exceptional rigor and ties that belief to prior work or design choices."}]}]}
